Remote (UK) | Full Time | Up to £70,000 DOE

Role Summary

Hours:
37.5 hours per week, with flexibility required
Salary:
Up to £70,000, depending on experience
Location:
Remote, UK-based
Start date:
January 2027

Role Overview

This is a senior role delivering complex operational projects and giving strategic oversight of a broader project portfolio. We’re looking for someone with substantial experience from a business process outsourcing (BPO) environment, or highly relevant transferable skills from another fast-paced, customer-focused operation.

You’ll work closely with stakeholders at every level, turning complex project and portfolio information into clear, concise reporting and recommendations for C-suite audiences. You’ll also guide our Project Managers through the full employee lifecycle, empowering them to take ownership, develop professionally and consistently deliver to high standards.

Establish and lead high-performing project teams, clarify accountabilities, develop robust delivery plans and secure the resources needed for success

At least five years’ experience at senior project management level, with a strong record of operational project delivery and portfolio governance

Substantial experience in a BPO environment or a closely related operational setting

jobs.description:
Back to jobs

Senior Customer Support Service Delivery Program Manager

San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States

In 1931, electrical draftsman Harry Beck looked at London’s Underground map and saw a system that had become too complicated to understand.

The maps at the time tried to represent the city geographically. Beck realized that wasn’t what riders actually needed. What mattered was how the system connected: which lines went where, where you could transfer, and the simplest way to get from one place to another. So he redrew the network around those relationships instead. His design became the foundation for the modern Tube map and changed how people navigated London.

Mercury’s Customer Experience organization has its own increasingly complex network.

As Mercury grows, the right place for support work will keep changing. Some new or complex work may benefit from starting in an incubation team before we know how it should scale. From there, it might move into Core Support, remain specialized, transition to an outsourced partner, or become increasingly supported by AI-powered tooling. The challenge is knowing where work belongs at each stage of its lifecycle, when it’s ready to move, and how to make those transitions without compromising the customer experience.

For the first 9–12 months, a significant majority of your work will focus on our growing BPO partnership. You’ll identify opportunities to expand the work we deliver through that partnership, build the operational and financial case for doing so, align CX leadership around those recommendations, and lead approved transitions from initial scoping through stabilization.

Over time, the scope will broaden. You’ll apply the same thinking across our wider service delivery ecosystem, helping us evaluate when work should enter an incubation model, when it is ready to graduate, and whether its next home should be Core Support, a specialized team, an outsourced partner, AI-powered tooling, or another model as our capabilities evolve.

You won’t be the sole decision-maker on where work lives. Your role is to develop the recommendation: bring together the data, customer impact, operational realities, and tradeoffs; build a compelling case; and help CX leadership reach a well-informed decision. Once a direction is approved, you’ll own the program that turns it into reality.

This is a role for someone who can move fluidly between strategy and execution. You should be equally energized by building a strong argument for how our service delivery model should evolve and by working through the operational details required to make that change succeed.

In This Role, You Will

Lead high-impact programs that evolve how CX delivers support, with the first 9–12 months heavily focused on expanding and optimizing our BPO partnership.
Identify opportunities to move work to a different service delivery model and build the case for change using customer, operational, and financial data. This could include recommending that emerging or complex work move into incubation, as well as determining when incubated work is mature enough to transition into Core Support, a specialized team, or our BPO partnership.
Help define what makes work ready to move. Develop clear criteria for when a workflow needs incubation, when it has reached sufficient maturity and stability to graduate, and which delivery model is best positioned to own it next.
Evaluate where AI-powered tooling could take on, augment, or reshape support work, and partner with the right teams to build a clear case for when automation creates a better customer and business outcome.
Lead approved service delivery transitions end to end, whether work is moving into incubation, graduating from incubation, transitioning between internal teams, or moving to an outsourced partner. Own the program from initial scoping and business case through readiness, migration, ramp, stabilization, and handoff into long-term operations.
Partner across Workforce Management, Enablement, QA, Support, and other teams to build transition plans that account for capacity, training, knowledge transfer, quality, tooling, and operational readiness.
Define success before a transition begins and measure whether the change actually delivered the intended customer, quality, capacity, and cost outcomes.
Establish clear readiness and stabilization criteria so transitions are judged by whether they work, not simply whether they launched on time.
Bring structure to complex, ambiguous service delivery questions, identifying the right analysis, stakeholders, dependencies, and tradeoffs required to move from uncertainty to a clear recommendation.
Build repeatable frameworks and approaches that make future service delivery decisions faster, clearer, and more consistent.
Use what we learn from each transition to continuously improve how Support evaluates where work should live and how changes should be executed.

We’re Looking For Someone Who

Has 6+ years of experience in strategic program management, customer experience operations, service delivery, outsourcing, support operations, or a related field.
Has deep experience with outsourced service delivery and has personally led significant transitions of operational work into a BPO or similar partner environment.
Understands the operational machinery behind successful BPO transitions, including workforce planning, forecasting, training, knowledge transfer, quality management, ramp planning, and stabilization.
Can build a strong recommendation without needing to own the final decision. You know how to gather the right evidence, frame tradeoffs clearly, anticipate objections, and create alignment among senior stakeholders.
Thinks in systems. You naturally look beyond the performance of an individual team to understand how the broader service delivery model works and where changing it could produce a better outcome.
Is analytically rigorous and commercially minded. You’re comfortable working with operational and financial data, testing assumptions, building business cases, and making recommendations when the answer isn’t obvious.
Exercises strong judgment in ambiguous environments. You can take a question like “Is this still the right place for this work?” and determine what evidence, tradeoffs, and perspectives are needed to answer it well.
Can move seamlessly from recommendation to execution. You’re as comfortable developing the case for a service delivery change as you are working through the details required to make it successful.
Influences effectively without relying on formal authority. You know how to align teams with different priorities and constraints around a shared outcome.
Communicates complex decisions with clarity. You can explain the customer impact, operational implications, economics, and tradeoffs behind a recommendation without burying the decision in the analysis.
Holds a high bar for outcomes, not just completion. You care whether a transition delivered what we expected and are willing to revisit assumptions when the data tells us otherwise.

The Ideal Candidate May Also Have

Experience designing or evolving a multi-tier customer support service delivery model.
Experience with BPO expansions, outsourced operations, vendor launches, or team and site stand-ups.
Experience moving work between different internal delivery models, such as from incubation to Core Support or between specialized and scaled support teams.
Experience evaluating how automation and AI-assisted support change the economics, complexity, or appropriate placement of customer support work.
Experience with incubation or pilot operating models, including determining when new or complex work should be isolated for learning and when it is ready to graduate into a scaled delivery environment.
Experience using SQL, Google Sheets, or business intelligence tools to evaluate operational performance and build business cases.
Experience in fintech, financial services, or another regulated environment where risk and operational complexity influence how work can be delivered.

Essential

Robust technical expertise with comprehensive knowledge of the automotive industry and software development.
A proactive problem-solving mindset.
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills.

A Master’s degree in Engineering or Computer Science.

Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. jobs.title: Information Security Manager
jobs.description:
While we welcome applications from everywhere, please note that at this stage we are prioritizing candidates who are already based in Stockholm and eligible to work in Sweden without visa sponsorship.

_______________________________

We are Bambuser, and we are reshaping commerce

Video has quickly become one of the most powerful ways for brands to engage, inspire, and convert consumers.
At Bambuser, we’re helping some of the world’s most recognized brands transform how they sell online through live shopping, shoppable video, and interactive commerce experiences. Brands including L’Oréal, Audi, Sephora, and Sonos use our platform to create richer and more engaging customer experiences.
As a global B2B SaaS company working with enterprise customers, trust matters at every stage of our business. Customers need to know that their data is handled responsibly. Teams need clear and practical guidance. Auditors need evidence that our controls work. As technology and regulation evolve, particularly around AI, our security practices need to keep pace.

That’s where you come in. ✨

_______________________________

About the role

Bambuser already has strong security foundations, including an ISO 27001-certified information security management system (ISMS). Your challenge will be to build on them as our business, customer expectations, and the regulatory landscape continue to evolve.
You’ll own our ISMS, including the information security Risk and Asset Registers, and partner with our General Counsel on the security side of privacy compliance. Day to day, you’ll help the business meet its regulatory obligations, keep our policies practical and current, and make sure we stay audit-ready year-round. Compliance and audit readiness are outcomes of doing security right, not ends in themselves.
We’re a fast-moving scale-up, so we need you to think the way we all try to think: what can be automated, templated, or scheduled instead of done by hand again? If you find yourself doing the same manual task twice, build the system that makes sure nobody has to do it a third time. The goal is to cut busywork, yours and everyone else’s, so time goes to the work that truly needs a human.
You’ll be part of our Operations team, reporting to the VP Operations and working closely with Legal, Engineering, IT Ops, and our commercial teams.

_______________________________

Main duties and responsibilities

ISMS Governance & Audit Readiness:
Own the ISO 27001 certification lifecycle and annual ISMS calendar, keeping recurring activities on track, from training and management reviews to nonconformities and corrective actions. Maintain the information security Risk and Asset Registers, keeping risks connected to business priorities. Run internal and external audits end to end: scoping, evidence collection, stakeholder coordination, and remediation.
Keeping policies sharp:
Own the full ISMS library and right-size policies to our actual risk profile. Build policies, playbooks, and control documentation that hold up under scrutiny and work in practice. Drive adoption through clear communication and practical guidance, so policies become part of how people work.
The face of security to customers & vendors:
Be the go-to contact for enterprise customer security reviews, RFP security sections, and the Trust Center. Lead the rollout of our RFP AI tool. On the procurement side, review new tools and vendors, including AI tools, for data handling, access, and integration risk before adoption.
Regulation, Privacy and AI:
Partner with Legal to track regulation across our markets and translate relevant requirements into concrete security controls with clear internal ownership. Support the security side of privacy compliance, including vendor data handling reviews and inputs to the Record of Processing Activities (ROPA) and Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs). Assess security risks associated with AI tools and help keep our AI usage guidelines current.
Security testing and training:
Coordinate penetration testing engagements with vendors and Engineering, from scoping and arranging access to tracking findings through remediation. Own our security awareness training program and content, designing and delivering onboarding and recurring sessions that stay relevant as threats and regulations shift.
Automation and ownership:
Turn security workflows into documented, automated processes. Work with IT Ops and other teams on evidence collection, control monitoring, training reminders, audit scheduling, and recurring tasks. Help teams understand and own their part in keeping Bambuser secure.

_______________________________

Requirements

Experience:
5+ years in information security compliance, IT audit, or risk management, ideally in B2B SaaS or another fast-growing tech company.
ISO 27001:
A track record of implementing or maintaining ISO/IEC 27001 certifications. Experience running or supporting penetration testing programs is a plus.
Privacy and regulation:
Strong working knowledge of GDPR and how security controls support privacy compliance in multi-tenant SaaS environments, plus an awareness of evolving AI regulation, including the EU AI Act, and its implications for a tech business.
Technical grounding:
Comfortable mapping systems, data flows, and integrations, and advising on the security implications of architecture changes.
Automation instinct:
Hands-on experience automating evidence collection or control monitoring and evaluating GRC platforms against building solutions in-house. Comfortable with workflow automation, scheduling tools, and AI-assisted drafting.
Pragmatism
: You turn complex requirements into workflows that don’t grind the business to a halt.
Communication:
You translate technical security risk into business terms, whether you’re speaking to executives, enterprise customers, or a room full of people at a training session.
Proactive and solutions-oriented:
You identify risks, spot patterns, and anticipate future needs, rather than waiting for problems to surface.
Bonus:
Experience working in or with publicly listed companies, including familiarity with their internal control requirements.

_______________________________

Why Bambuser?

You’ll join a focused, hungry team that enjoys working together and getting things done. We move quickly, help one another, and give people room to take ownership.
Here, your contribution will be visible and felt across the company. You’ll help teams make informed decisions, build trust with enterprise customers, and create security practices that support how we grow.
You’ll have solid foundations to build on, an experienced team around you, and the opportunity to shape how information security works at Bambuser.

Senior Customer Support Service Delivery Program Manager

In 1931, electrical draftsman Harry Beck looked at London’s Underground map and saw a system that had become too complicated to understand.

The maps at the time tried to represent the city geographically. Beck realized that wasn’t what riders actually needed. What mattered was how the system connected: which lines went where, where you could transfer, and the simplest way to get from one place to another. So he redrew the network around those relationships instead. His design became the foundation for the modern Tube map and changed how people navigated London.

Mercury’s Customer Experience organization has its own increasingly complex network.

As Mercury grows, the right place for support work will keep changing. Some new or complex work may benefit from starting in an incubation team before we know how it should scale. From there, it might move into Core Support, remain specialized, transition to an outsourced partner, or become increasingly supported by AI-powered tooling. The challenge is knowing where work belongs at each stage of its lifecycle, when it’s ready to move, and how to make those transitions without compromising the customer experience.

For the first 9–12 months, a significant majority of your work will focus on our growing BPO partnership. You’ll identify opportunities to expand the work we deliver through that partnership, build the operational and financial case for doing so, align CX leadership around those recommendations, and lead approved transitions from initial scoping through stabilization.

Over time, the scope will broaden. You’ll apply the same thinking across our wider service delivery ecosystem, helping us evaluate when work should enter an incubation model, when it is ready to graduate, and whether its next home should be Core Support, a specialized team, an outsourced partner, AI-powered tooling, or another model as our capabilities evolve.

You won’t be the sole decision-maker on where work lives. Your role is to develop the recommendation: bring together the data, customer impact, operational realities, and tradeoffs; build a compelling case; and help CX leadership reach a well-informed decision. Once a direction is approved, you’ll own the program that turns it into reality.

This is a role for someone who can move fluidly between strategy and execution. You should be equally energized by building a strong argument for how our service delivery model should evolve and by working through the operational details required to make that change succeed.

In This Role, You Will

Lead high-impact programs that evolve how CX delivers support, with the first 9–12 months heavily focused on expanding and optimizing our BPO partnership.
Identify opportunities to move work to a different service delivery model and build the case for change using customer, operational, and financial data. This could include recommending that emerging or complex work move into incubation, as well as determining when incubated work is mature enough to transition into Core Support, a specialized team, or our BPO partnership.
Help define what makes work ready to move. Develop clear criteria for when a workflow needs incubation, when it has reached sufficient maturity and stability to graduate, and which delivery model is best positioned to own it next.
Evaluate where AI-powered tooling could take on, augment, or reshape support work, and partner with the right teams to build a clear case for when automation creates a better customer and business outcome.
Lead approved service delivery transitions end to end, whether work is moving into incubation, graduating from incubation, transitioning between internal teams, or moving to an outsourced partner. Own the program from initial scoping and business case through readiness, migration, ramp, stabilization, and handoff into long-term operations.
Partner across Workforce Management, Enablement, QA, Support, and other teams to build transition plans that account for capacity, training, knowledge transfer, quality, tooling, and operational readiness.
Define success before a transition begins and measure whether the change actually delivered the intended customer, quality, capacity, and cost outcomes.
Establish clear readiness and stabilization criteria so transitions are judged by whether they work, not simply whether they launched on time.
Bring structure to complex, ambiguous service delivery questions, identifying the right analysis, stakeholders, dependencies, and tradeoffs required to move from uncertainty to a clear recommendation.
Build repeatable frameworks and approaches that make future service delivery decisions faster, clearer, and more consistent.
Use what we learn from each transition to continuously improve how Support evaluates where work should live and how changes should be executed.

We’re Looking For Someone Who

Has 6+ years of experience in strategic program management, customer experience operations, service delivery, outsourcing, support operations, or a related field.
Has deep experience with outsourced service delivery and has personally led significant transitions of operational work into a BPO or similar partner environment.
Understands the operational machinery behind successful BPO transitions, including workforce planning, forecasting, training, knowledge transfer, quality management, ramp planning, and stabilization.
Can build a strong recommendation without needing to own the final decision. You know how to gather the right evidence, frame tradeoffs clearly, anticipate objections, and create alignment among senior stakeholders.
Thinks in systems. You naturally look beyond the performance of an individual team to understand how the broader service delivery model works and where changing it could produce a better outcome.
Is analytically rigorous and commercially minded. You’re comfortable working with operational and financial data, testing assumptions, building business cases, and making recommendations when the answer isn’t obvious.
Exercises strong judgment in ambiguous environments. You can take a question like “Is this still the right place for this work?” and determine what evidence, tradeoffs, and perspectives are needed to answer it well.
Can move seamlessly from recommendation to execution. You’re as comfortable developing the case for a service delivery change as you are working through the details required to make it successful.
Influences effectively without relying on formal authority. You know how to align teams with different priorities and constraints around a shared outcome.
Communicates complex decisions with clarity. You can explain the customer impact, operational implications, economics, and tradeoffs behind a recommendation without burying the decision in the analysis.
Holds a high bar for outcomes, not just completion. You care whether a transition delivered what we expected and are willing to revisit assumptions when the data tells us otherwise.

The Ideal Candidate May Also Have

Experience designing or evolving a multi-tier customer support service delivery model.
Experience with BPO expansions, outsourced operations, vendor launches, or team and site stand-ups.
Experience moving work between different internal delivery models, such as from incubation to Core Support or between specialized and scaled support teams.
Experience evaluating how automation and AI-assisted support change the economics, complexity, or appropriate placement of customer support work.
Experience with incubation or pilot operating models, including determining when new or complex work should be isolated for learning and when it is ready to graduate into a scaled delivery environment.
Experience using SQL, Google Sheets, or business intelligence tools to evaluate operational performance and build business cases.
Experience in fintech, financial services, or another regulated environment where risk and operational complexity influence how work can be delivered.

_______________________________

We are Bambuser, and we are reshaping commerce

Video has quickly become one of the most powerful ways for brands to engage, inspire, and convert consumers.
At Bambuser, we’re helping some of the world’s most recognized brands transform how they sell online through live shopping, shoppable video, and interactive commerce experiences. Brands including L’Oréal, Audi, Sephora, and Sonos use our platform to create richer and more engaging customer experiences.
As a global B2B SaaS company working with enterprise customers, trust matters at every stage of our business. Customers need to know that their data is handled responsibly. Teams need clear and practical guidance. Auditors need evidence that our controls work. As technology and regulation evolve, particularly around AI, our security practices need to keep pace.

That’s where you come in. ✨

_______________________________

About the role

Bambuser already has strong security foundations, including an ISO 27001-certified information security management system (ISMS). Your challenge will be to build on them as our business, customer expectations, and the regulatory landscape continue to evolve.
You’ll own our ISMS, including the information security Risk and Asset Registers, and partner with our General Counsel on the security side of privacy compliance. Day to day, you’ll help the business meet its regulatory obligations, keep our policies practical and current, and make sure we stay audit-ready year-round. Compliance and audit readiness are outcomes of doing security right, not ends in themselves.
We’re a fast-moving scale-up, so we need you to think the way we all try to think: what can be automated, templated, or scheduled instead of done by hand again? If you find yourself doing the same manual task twice, build the system that makes sure nobody has to do it a third time. The goal is to cut busywork, yours and everyone else’s, so time goes to the work that truly needs a human.
You’ll be part of our Operations team, reporting to the VP Operations and working closely with Legal, Engineering, IT Ops, and our commercial teams.

_______________________________

Main duties and responsibilities

ISMS Governance & Audit Readiness:
Own the ISO 27001 certification lifecycle and annual ISMS calendar, keeping recurring activities on track, from training and management reviews to nonconformities and corrective actions. Maintain the information security Risk and Asset Registers, keeping risks connected to business priorities. Run internal and external audits end to end: scoping, evidence collection, stakeholder coordination, and remediation.
Keeping policies sharp:
Own the full ISMS library and right-size policies to our actual risk profile. Build policies, playbooks, and control documentation that hold up under scrutiny and work in practice. Drive adoption through clear communication and practical guidance, so policies become part of how people work.
The face of security to customers & vendors:
Be the go-to contact for enterprise customer security reviews, RFP security sections, and the Trust Center. Lead the rollout of our RFP AI tool. On the procurement side, review new tools and vendors, including AI tools, for data handling, access, and integration risk before adoption.
Regulation, Privacy and AI:
Partner with Legal to track regulation across our markets and translate relevant requirements into concrete security controls with clear internal ownership. Support the security side of privacy compliance, including vendor data handling reviews and inputs to the Record of Processing Activities (ROPA) and Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs). Assess security risks associated with AI tools and help keep our AI usage guidelines current.
Security testing and training:
Coordinate penetration testing engagements with vendors and Engineering, from scoping and arranging access to tracking findings through remediation. Own our security awareness training program and content, designing and delivering onboarding and recurring sessions that stay relevant as threats and regulations shift.
Automation and ownership:
Turn security workflows into documented, automated processes. Work with IT Ops and other teams on evidence collection, control monitoring, training reminders, audit scheduling, and recurring tasks. Help teams understand and own their part in keeping Bambuser secure.

_______________________________

Requirements

Experience:
5+ years in information security compliance, IT audit, or risk management, ideally in B2B SaaS or another fast-growing tech company.
ISO 27001:
A track record of implementing or maintaining ISO/IEC 27001 certifications. Experience running or supporting penetration testing programs is a plus.
Privacy and regulation:
Strong working knowledge of GDPR and how security controls support privacy compliance in multi-tenant SaaS environments, plus an awareness of evolving AI regulation, including the EU AI Act, and its implications for a tech business.
Technical grounding:
Comfortable mapping systems, data flows, and integrations, and advising on the security implications of architecture changes.
Automation instinct:
Hands-on experience automating evidence collection or control monitoring and evaluating GRC platforms against building solutions in-house. Comfortable with workflow automation, scheduling tools, and AI-assisted drafting.
Pragmatism
: You turn complex requirements into workflows that don’t grind the business to a halt.
Communication:
You translate technical security risk into business terms, whether you’re speaking to executives, enterprise customers, or a room full of people at a training session.
Proactive and solutions-oriented:
You identify risks, spot patterns, and anticipate future needs, rather than waiting for problems to surface.
